sbh2.6:1.2: Mindfulness having in-and-out-breaths as its object — this is called *ānāpānasmṛti*.
sbh2.6:2.5: The in-breath is the air that, immediately after the out-breath, moves inward as far as the navel region.
sbh2.6:2.6: The inner-in-breath is, when this in-breath has ceased and the out-breath has not yet arisen, the brief wind resembling it that arises at the resting-place in the interval.
sbh2.6:2.8: The out-breath and inner-out-breath should be understood likewise.
sbh2.6:2.10: the air moves outward from the navel region as far as the tip of the mouth or nose, and from there outside.
sbh2.6:3.1: There are two causes of in-and-out-breaths.
sbh2.6:3.3: The relevant kind of karma, and the cavity of the navel region;
sbh2.6:3.4: or alternatively, the cavity of the body that arises from this.
sbh2.6:3.5: What are the two supports of in-and-out-breathing?
sbh2.6:3.9: and that as is appropriate. If they proceeded body-supported only,
sbh2.6:3.10: they would proceed in beings attained to the unconscious attainment, the cessation attainment, and in beings born among the unconscious gods.
sbh2.6:3.12: they would proceed in beings who have attained the formless [attainments] or are born in the formless [realms].
sbh2.6:3.13: If they proceeded body-supported and mind-supported,
sbh2.6:3.14: but not as is appropriate, they would proceed in beings attained to or born in the fourth absorption, and in beings in the *kalala* (zygote), *arbuda* (early embryo), and *peśī* (fleshy mass) stages of gestation.
sbh2.6:3.15: But they do not so proceed.
sbh2.6:3.16: Therefore in-and-out-breaths proceed body-supported and mind-supported, and that as is appropriate.

sbh2.6:4.5: The two abodes of the breaths:

sbh2.6:4.8: The gross cavity is from the navel region as far as the door of mouth-and-nose,
sbh2.6:4.9: and from the door of mouth-and-nose as far as the navel cavity.
sbh2.6:4.11: All the pores of the body.

sbh2.6:6.1: Two faults [arise] for one engaged with the in-and-out-breaths.
sbh2.6:6.4: In [Conjectural: over-slack] engagement, falling into laziness, the mind is enveloped by sloth-and-torpor or distracted outwardly.
sbh2.6:6.5: In over-tight engagement, bodily disturbance arises,
sbh2.6:6.8: For one who presses the in-and-out-breaths by forceful restraint, irregular airs proceed in the body.
sbh2.6:6.9: They first stir in such-and-such limbs and minor limbs;
sbh2.6:6.11: When these throbbing airs grow, they become *rujakas* (paining airs);
sbh2.6:6.12: and these, moreover, produce pain in those limbs and minor limbs.
sbh2.6:6.16: or is overcome by [Conjectural: severe] dejection and distress.
sbh2.6:7.1: Five familiarities of this *ānāpānasmṛti* should be known:
sbh2.6:7.2: counting-familiarity, aggregate-entry-familiarity, dependent-origination-entry-familiarity, truth-entry-familiarity, and sixteen-aspect-familiarity.
sbh2.6:9.3: with mindfulness bound to the in-and-out-breath, he counts 'one.'
sbh2.6:9.4: When the in-breath has ceased and the out-breath arises and goes out,
sbh2.6:9.5: he counts 'two.' Thus he counts up to ten.
sbh2.6:9.6: This counting is neither too compressed nor too extended. This is called one-by-one counting.
sbh2.6:9.8: When the in-breath has entered and ceased,
sbh2.6:9.11: By this method of counting he counts up to ten.
sbh2.6:9.13: He combines in-and-out into a single unit and counts it as one — thus called two-as-one counting.
sbh2.6:9.15: By either one-by-one counting or two-as-one counting, he counts forward up to ten.
sbh2.6:9.18: Starting from ten in reverse — nine, eight, seven, six, five — down to one.
sbh2.6:9.20: When, relying on one-by-one counting or two-as-one counting, he has made familiarity with forward and reverse counting,
sbh2.6:9.21: and the mind does not become distracted in the meantime,
sbh2.6:9.23: then the further, superior counting is prescribed for him.
sbh2.6:9.25: By either one-by-one or two-as-one counting, he makes two-as-one and counts.
sbh2.6:9.26: By two-as-one counting, four in-and-out-breaths are one unit.
sbh2.6:9.27: By one-by-one counting, an in-and-out pair is one. Thus he counts up to ten.
sbh2.6:9.28: By such progressive enlargement, he eventually makes a hundred breaths one unit and counts.
sbh2.6:9.29: Then by hundred-as-one counting in sequence he counts up to ten.
sbh2.6:9.30: When this counting-engaged practitioner makes ten-as-one and counts up to ten —
sbh2.6:9.31: as long as he fulfills the ten —
sbh2.6:9.32: by this ten-as-one counting the mind does not become distracted [Conjectural: in the meantime].
sbh2.6:9.33: By this much, his counting-familiarity is accomplished.
sbh2.6:9.34: Of this counting-engaged practitioner, if the mind becomes distracted in the meantime, he turns back and starts counting again from the beginning,
sbh2.6:9.36: When his mind, [Conjectural: through thorough familiarity], of its own accord, mounted on the very path that flows of itself, bound to the in-and-out-breath object, proceeds unbroken and uninterrupted — grasping the in-breath as it proceeds, grasping the state empty of out-breath when the in-breath has ceased, grasping the out-breath as it proceeds, grasping its cessation when it has ceased — unwavering, unmoving, without the aspect of distraction, and with delight —
sbh2.6:9.37: by this much the counting-stage is transcended.
sbh2.6:9.38: Then no more counting is to be done.
sbh2.6:9.39: Mind is no longer bound to any object other than the in-and-out-breaths.
sbh2.6:9.40: The in-and-out-breaths — together with the inner in-breaths and inner out-breaths, and with their states of proceeding and ceasing — are to be followed and characterized.
sbh2.6:9.42: This counting-familiarity is prescribed for those of dull faculties.
sbh2.6:9.43: For them this [counting] serves, [Conjectural: where there is distraction],
sbh2.6:9.44: for the abiding of the mind and for the mind's delight;
sbh2.6:9.45: otherwise, without counting, sloth-and-torpor would envelop their mind, or the mind would be distracted outwardly; but for them, engaged in counting, this does not happen.
sbh2.6:9.46: But those of sharp faculties, with keen understanding, have [Conjectural: no] liking for taking up the counting-practice.
sbh2.6:9.47: Once instructed, they penetrate the counting-engagement very quickly,
sbh2.6:9.48: and do not find delight in it.
sbh2.6:9.49: They bind mindfulness to the in-and-out-breath object, and where they proceed, how far they proceed, in what manner they proceed, and when they proceed —
sbh2.6:9.50: all of this they follow and characterize with established mindfulness.
sbh2.6:9.51: This is the form of their engagement.
sbh2.6:9.52: Through familiarization, cultivation, and frequent practice of this engagement, bodily pliancy and mental pliancy arise.
sbh2.6:9.53: He attains one-pointedness and comes to delight in the object.
sbh2.6:10.1: He who has thus made counting-familiarity, by attending to the grasper-and-grasped thing, enters the aggregates.
sbh2.6:10.2: The in-and-out-breaths, and that body which is their basis — attending to these, he enters the form-aggregate.
sbh2.6:10.3: The experience-and-undergoing of those in-and-out-breaths, conjoined with the mindfulness that grasps them — this he enters as the feeling-aggregate.
sbh2.6:10.4: The cognizing of them — this he enters as the perception-aggregate.
sbh2.6:10.5: The mindfulness, the volition, and the discernment present here —
sbh2.6:10.6: this he enters as the formations-aggregate.
sbh2.6:10.7: The mind, mentation, consciousness — this he enters as the consciousness-aggregate.
sbh2.6:10.9: thus having entered the aggregates — this is called aggregate-entry-familiarity.
sbh2.6:11.1: When through this he has seen mere aggregate,
sbh2.6:11.2: fully understood it as mere formation, mere thing, then he enters the dependent origination of these very formations.
sbh2.6:11.4: He searches and seeks: 'These in-and-out-breaths — supported by what? Conditioned by what?'
sbh2.6:11.5: It occurs to him: 'These in-and-out-breaths are body-supported, body-conditioned; mind-supported, mind-conditioned.
sbh2.6:11.6: The body and the mind — what are they conditioned by?'
sbh2.6:11.7: He enters: 'The body and the mind are conditioned by the life-faculty.' [Lacuna]
sbh2.6:11.8: The previous formation — [Conjectural: what is it conditioned by?]
sbh2.6:11.9: he enters: 'The previous formation is conditioned by ignorance.'
sbh2.6:11.10: Thus: the previous formation is conditioned by ignorance; the life-faculty is conditioned by [Conjectural: the previous] formation; body and consciousness are conditioned by the life-faculty; the in-and-out-breaths are conditioned by body-and-mind.
sbh2.6:11.11: From the cessation of ignorance, cessation of formations.
sbh2.6:11.12: From the cessation of formations, cessation of the life-faculty.
sbh2.6:11.13: From the cessation of the life-faculty, cessation of body-and-mind.
sbh2.6:11.14: From the cessation of body-and-mind, cessation of in-and-out-breaths.
sbh2.6:11.16: Frequently abiding in this, he is said to have made familiarity in the dependent-origination aspect.
sbh2.6:12.1: Having thus made familiarity in dependent origination: 'These formations which are dependently arisen —
sbh2.6:12.3: Because of impermanence, not having been [Conjectural: they come to be, and having come to be] they pass away.
sbh2.6:12.4: Again, not having been, they come to be;
sbh2.6:12.5: having come to be, they pass away.
sbh2.6:12.6: They are subject to birth, aging, illness, death.
sbh2.6:12.7: What is subject to birth, aging, illness, death — that is suffering. What is suffering — that is not-self, not autonomous, devoid of master.
sbh2.6:12.8: Thus by the aspects of impermanent, suffering, empty, and not-self, he has entered the truth of suffering.
sbh2.6:12.9: Whatever arising there is of these formations —
sbh2.6:12.10: that is suffering, is disease, is a boil; all of it conditioned by craving.
sbh2.6:12.11: Whatever is the complete abandoning of this craving that gives rise to suffering: 'This is peace, this is excellent. Knowing this thus and abiding frequently thus, the complete abandoning of craving will come to be for me.'
sbh2.6:12.12: Thus he enters the truth of arising, the truth of cessation, and the truth of the path.
sbh2.6:12.13: Frequently abiding in this — when he realizes the truths —
sbh2.6:13.1: For one who has thus made familiarity in the truths,
sbh2.6:13.2: with the abandoning of dharmas to be abandoned by seeing, the dharmas to be abandoned by cultivation remain.
sbh2.6:13.3: For their abandoning, he makes the sixteen-aspect-familiarity.
sbh2.6:14.2: Mindful while breathing in: he trains 'I breathe in mindful.'
sbh2.6:14.3: Mindful while breathing out: he trains 'I breathe out mindful.'
sbh2.6:14.4: Long. Short. Experiencing the whole body.
sbh2.6:14.5: Breathing in experiencing the whole body, he trains 'I breathe in experiencing the whole body.'
sbh2.6:14.6: Breathing out experiencing the whole body,
sbh2.6:14.7: he trains 'I breathe out experiencing the whole body.'
sbh2.6:14.8: Calming the body-conditioner, breathing in, he trains 'I breathe in calming the body-conditioner.'
sbh2.6:14.9: Calming the body-conditioner, breathing out, he trains 'I breathe out calming the body-conditioner.'
sbh2.6:14.10: Experiencing rapture; experiencing happiness — he trains.
sbh2.6:14.11: Experiencing the mind-conditioner; calming the mind-conditioner, breathing in: he trains 'I breathe in calming the mind-conditioner.'
sbh2.6:14.12: Calming the mind-conditioner, breathing out, he trains 'I breathe out calming the mind-conditioner.'
sbh2.6:14.14: Gladdening the mind; concentrating the mind; liberating the mind, breathing in: he trains 'I breathe in liberating the mind.'
sbh2.6:14.15: Liberating the mind, breathing out, he trains 'I breathe out liberating the mind.'
sbh2.6:14.16: Contemplating impermanence; contemplating abandoning; contemplating dispassion; breathing in: he trains 'I breathe in contemplating cessation.'
sbh2.6:14.17: Contemplating cessation, breathing out, he trains 'I breathe out contemplating cessation.'
sbh2.6:15.1: What is the distinction of these?
sbh2.6:15.3: the trainee who has [Conjectural: seen the footing] is an obtainer
sbh2.6:15.4: of the four foundations of mindfulness, and, with the in-and-out-breath as object,
sbh2.6:15.6: for the abandoning of the remaining fetters.
sbh2.6:15.8: Breathing in, he trains 'I breathe in mindful.'
sbh2.6:15.9: When he takes the in-breath or out-breath as object, he trains 'I breathe in long, I breathe out long.'
sbh2.6:15.10: When he makes the inner-in-breath or inner-out-breath the object,
sbh2.6:15.11: he trains 'I breathe in short, I breathe out short.'
sbh2.6:15.12: Thus indeed the in-and-out-breaths proceed long;
sbh2.6:15.13: the inner-in-breaths and inner-out-breaths are short, and proceed accordingly.
sbh2.6:15.16: When he resolves upon the in-and-out-breaths as having reached the subtle cavity and entered into diffusion throughout the body,
sbh2.6:15.17: he makes [the whole body] the object.
sbh2.6:15.18: When the out-breath and the inner-out-breath have ceased,
sbh2.6:15.19: and the in-breath and the inner-in-breath have not yet arisen,
sbh2.6:15.20: he makes the state empty of out-breath and in-breath — removed from them, separated from them [Damaged] — the object.
sbh2.6:15.21: At that time, calming the body-conditioner, breathing in — he trains 'I breathe in calming the body-conditioner.'
sbh2.6:15.22: Calming the body-conditioner, breathing out, he trains 'I breathe out calming the body-conditioner.'
sbh2.6:15.23: Moreover, through his familiarization, cultivation, and frequent practice —
sbh2.6:15.24: those rough, unpleasant-to-touch in-and-out-breaths that proceeded for one not previously familiarized —
sbh2.6:15.25: for the familiarized one, other breaths proceed, soft and pleasant to the touch.
sbh2.6:15.26: Therefore he says, 'calming the body-conditioner, I breathe in' — he trains.
sbh2.6:16.1: Engaged in *ānāpānasmṛti* in this manner, if he is one who attains
sbh2.6:16.2: the first or the second absorption — at that time, 'experiencing rapture, breathing in, he trains: experiencing rapture, I breathe in.'
sbh2.6:16.3: If he is one who attains
sbh2.6:16.5: at that time he is 'experiencing happiness.'
sbh2.6:16.6: Beyond the third absorption, *ānāpānasmṛti* is no longer applicable.
sbh2.6:16.7: Hence [the practice] is declared to be comprised as far as the third absorption.
sbh2.6:17.1: Of this practitioner — experiencing rapture, or experiencing happiness —
sbh2.6:17.2: if at some time or other, from a lapse of mindfulness, there arises [the thought]:
sbh2.6:17.3: 'I am,' or 'this very I am,' 'I shall be' or 'I shall not be,' 'I shall be with form, I shall be without form,'
sbh2.6:17.5: 'I shall be neither percipient nor non-percipient' — when in this way there arises, accompanied by deluded perception and volition, stirring, [Conjectural: conceiving], proliferation, fabrication, craving,
sbh2.6:17.6: that which has arisen, he penetrates quickly with discernment.
sbh2.6:17.11: Thus, 'experiencing the mind-conditioner, calming the mind-conditioner, breathing in, I breathe in calming the mind-conditioner' — he trains.
sbh2.6:18.1: If he attains the basic first, second, or third absorption — and he is then necessarily an attainer of the *anāgamya*, the preparatory stage of the first absorption —
sbh2.6:18.2: taking that as support, he reviews his arisen mind:
sbh2.6:18.3: with passion or without passion; with hatred or without; with delusion or without; contracted, sunk, uplifted, agitated or not agitated, calmed or not calmed, concentrated or not concentrated, well-cultivated or not well-cultivated, liberated or not liberated — thus he knows the mind as it actually is.
sbh2.6:18.6: When the mind has sunk into the hindrance of sloth-and-torpor
sbh2.6:18.7: as he is collecting [it] inwardly — then he displays one or another gladdening object,
sbh2.6:18.12: When he sees that it is [Conjectural: covered] by the hindrance of agitation or the hindrance of remorse
sbh2.6:18.13: as he is exerting [it] too far — then he displays one or another gladdening object and settles it inwardly.
sbh2.6:18.16: When through familiarization, cultivation, and frequent practice that mind has become distanced from the active occurrence of hindrances,
sbh2.6:18.18: therefore 'liberating the mind, breathing in, I breathe in liberating the mind' — he trains.
sbh2.6:19.1: Of the one whose mind is liberated from the hindrances obstructive to path-cultivation, the latent tendencies remain.
sbh2.6:19.3: For their abandoning, he brings the path to presence — namely, he examines carefully, properly, and methodically the impermanence of formations.
sbh2.6:19.5: Previously, there was *śamatha* engagement supported by the first, second, or third absorption, or by the *anāgamya*.
sbh2.6:19.6: Now he applies himself directly to the *vipaśyanā* of contemplating impermanence. Thus his mind, perfumed by *śamatha-vipaśyanā*, is liberated in the elements,
sbh2.6:19.9: The element of abandoning, the element of dispassion, and the element of cessation.
sbh2.6:19.10: The abandoning of all formations to be abandoned by seeing — that is the abandoning-element.
sbh2.6:19.11: The abandoning of all formations to be abandoned by cultivation — that is the dispassion-element.
sbh2.6:19.12: The cessation of all bases of clinging — that is the cessation-element.
sbh2.6:19.13: Thus, attending to the three elements as peace, as security, as health, he cultivates *śamatha-vipaśyanā*.
sbh2.6:19.14: Through familiarization, cultivation, and frequent practice, the mind is liberated from the remaining cultivation-abandonable defilements.
sbh2.6:19.15: Therefore 'contemplating abandoning, contemplating dispassion, contemplating cessation, breathing in, I breathe in contemplating cessation' — he trains.
sbh2.6:20.1: Thus, when the defilements abandonable by seeing and by cultivation
sbh2.6:20.2: have been abandoned, he becomes an arhat,
sbh2.6:20.3: one whose outflows are exhausted. There is nothing further to be done by him.
sbh2.6:20.4: nor any [Conjectural: adding to] what has been done.

sbh2.6:21.3: [Conjectural: where there is distraction], [it is] inward, one's own, very near — whereby for one engaging there, the agitation of applied thought does not arise.
sbh2.6:21.4: The mind quickly settles on the object;
sbh2.6:21.7: This is the fivefold conduct-purifying object for the applied-thought-conduct person.
